statement: Seven numbers have a mean of 12. One of them, $x$, is replaced by $3x$, and the mean of the seven numbers becomes 14. What is $x$?

choices.misconception: I found how much the total went up, 14, and gave that as $x$, forgetting the increase is $3x - x = 2x$.
I thought the number itself went up by 2, the same as the mean, so I solved $2x = 2$.
I found the new number $3x$ instead of the original number $x$.
I thought the total went up by $3x$ instead of by $3x - x$, so I solved $3x = 14$.

hints: How much did the total of the seven numbers go up?
Turn both means into totals. The change in the total comes only from replacing $x$ by $3x$, so compare the increase in the total with $3x - x$.
The total rose from $7 \times 12 = 84$ to $7 \times 14 = 98$, an increase of 14.

solutions.reliable: The total was $7 \times 12 = 84$ and becomes $7 \times 14 = 98$, so it rose by 14. Replacing $x$ by $3x$ raises the total by $3x - x = 2x$, so $2x = 14$ and $x = 7$. Check: changing 7 to 21 adds 14 to the total. The transferable idea: a change in the mean times the count gives the change in the total.

whyOnTest: Means questions test converting between means and totals; here the trap is mixing up the increase in the total with the number itself.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
